saints.name: St. Bede the Venerable
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The monk of Jarrow whose history first told the story of the English Church, the “Father of English History”…
biography: Bede was born about 673 on the lands of Wearmouth monastery in Northumbria, and at seven was given by his kinsfolk to Abbot Benedict Biscop, and afterwards to Ceolfrith of Jarrow. In that twin monastery he passed his whole life, as he wrote, amid the observance of the Rule and the daily singing of the Church, delighting to learn, to teach, or to write.

Ordained deacon at nineteen and priest at thirty by St. John of Beverley, he poured out commentaries on Scripture and treatises on chronology and the natural order. His crown is the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, finished in 731, which gathered ancient documents, the traditions of elders, and his own knowledge into the chief source for the conversion of England, whence he is called the Father of English History.

Dying on the vigil of the Ascension, 26 May 735, he dictated an English rendering of St. John's Gospel; when the boy Wilbert wrote the last sentence, Bede answered, 'It is finished,' and breathed his last singing the Glory be. Within two generations he was styled Venerable; Leo XIII declared him Doctor of the Church in 1899, and he is patron of historians and scholars.
saints.knownFor: His Ecclesiastical History of the English People.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1899)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 May
